Question: If you wrote a love letter to yourself, what would it say?
Answer: I’ve never said this to any girl but I’ll say this to you— I love you. I love you more than my sister. More than my parents. And more than anyone who was born before or after you. It took me long to accept you. It took me long to love you. I treated you bad for years. I ended you, almost, and I’ll regret that for the rest of my life. No one stood for you in your bad times, despite knowing what you were going through. Not your friends. Not your family. But you managed to escape it on your own. And for that, I’ve deep respect for you. It’s something I’m very proud of. I know the scars still haunt you. But that’s okay. Life shouldn’t be easy like a joke. You were a crying baby then. You used to cry like a newborn when you got hurt. But some incidents changed you. Some people changed you. Remember, when you sat with me alone in the darkroom and convinced me that it’s not okay to cry? It’s a shame, you said. Why, I asked. To which you replied— No one deserves your tears. I repeat, no one. They think it’s too common to cry. They don’t think you’re crying for life. They don’t think something’s killing you from inside and it might actually kill you. Like literally. So you turned into a rock. Not to people. But to yourself. And I won’t blame you for that. I know this love letter turned out to be a complete melancholy. Though it’s not my fault. All your close ones know just the good part of you. Earlier you easily opened up to people. But now you think no one deserves to hear the dark side of you. No one, except me. And that’s why I love you. I love you more than my life. And I’ll never take you for granted, ever. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Why are a lot of writers/poets sad?
Answer: Everyone thinks Jaun Eliya was an actor, a performer. But not just him—people believe that all writers who craft dark fiction are happy-go-lucky individuals, penning oddities merely to sell their books. Yet, name one good piece of fiction that doesn't have a melancholic side to it. As the classic writer Leo Tolstoy wrote in Anna Karenina: All happy families are alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way. Sadness has various spectrums. If you've gone through a breakup and believe you've recovered, you're not done yet. Someday, one of your closest family members will pass away, leaving you devastated. Just when you think you've healed, you might find yourself financially broken. Then come diseases, family problems, toxic friendships, oppressive work cultures, abusive partners, rape, crime, suicide, depression, natural calamities, and countless other miseries. Writers are not pessimists; they are self-healers. If you haven't inked your sorrows onto paper yet, you'll remain unaware of how liberating writing can be. People celebrate when they're happy. They love to be surrounded by others during the best times of their lives. But when melancholy strikes, when they can no longer bear the weight, they turn inward. No one wants to be in public when they're lonely. They seek solitude. They want to bleed words, and that’s when a masterpiece is born. Writing is a lonely process. But does that make the writer a loner? Well, that’s a story for another time. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What horrible thing you read today shocked you?
Answer: I had 7 kids with my own daughter. The case of Josef Fritzl is one of the most disturbing in recent history. Fritzl imprisoned his daughter, Elisabeth, in a secret cellar beneath their home in Amstetten for 24 years. During her captivity, he mistreated her, leading to the birth of seven children. Elisabeth had been missing since 1984, and her absence was a mystery to her family and community. Fritzl had lured her into the cellar under the guise of needing help with a household task, then drugged and handcuffed her. Over the years, he constructed an elaborate network of rooms in the cellar, soundproofed and concealed from the outside world. The crime was discovered in 2008 when one of Elisabeth's children, who had never seen sunlight, fell seriously ill and required urgent medical attention. Fritzl took the child to the hospital, sparking suspicions and eventually leading to a police investigation. Elisabeth, along with her other children, was found in the hidden basement, revealing the extent of Fritzl's horrific actions. I watched this tale on YouTube the moment after I woke up today. Disturbing. Horrifying. Unbelievable. It's weird how this world could be a calk-walk for an individual and an absolute nightmare for the other. We don't know each others stories. We have no clue what someone has gone through in the past and is still going through. Yet, when we see them a bit cut off from the people, we judge them. There are a hundred type of sadness. Each has their own magnitude. And if you’re not going through any of them, currently, be grateful. And empathize. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: You only realize the importance of someone when they are gone. Is this true?
Answer: My ex lives in Delhi. Three students died there yesterday due to flooding, and I was concerned for her. “Hello,” I said over the call. “I just heard the news about the students. Are you safe?” “Yes. How are you?” “Good. Do you go outside? If you do, please don't until everything settles down.” “Yes,” she replied. “I do go outside for work. I've got a new part-time job here. But I might need to stop now, maybe.” “Please search for any work-from-home setup.” We started discussing novels then. It has always been like that. We could never stop talking about books when we were together, and that hasn't changed much. She becomes so excited when talking about novels. “The Bell Jar,” she said. “Oh my world. I understand now why you were stopping me from reading that novel.” The conversation was about to end when she asked if I was still single. “That’s so strange,” I laughed. “Why are you laughing?” “I wanted to tell you the same, and you asked first. Yes,” I said. “I’m seeing someone.” A melancholic silence followed. I couldn't say anything further. I asked if she had found someone as well, to which she replied no. “I’m not seeing anyone,” she took a long pause and continued. “Okay. I need to go now. Bye.” “Bye.” She's still there. We still talk to each other once in a while. I have lost her as a girlfriend, yes, but not as a person. I valued her before. I value her now. It's just that we couldn't be together romantically. Question: What do you really want? Why do you want it?
Answer: I want for my story to be unique. I don't get influenced easily by others. I don't follow a single master or worship a hero. This isn't an issue of ego; it's simply how I've always chosen to live my life. Influencers are the biggest scam. They don't offer the truth or reveal the struggles they endure. You only see the perks of their lives and consequently resent your own. Take this example: On social media, my hair looks perfect, and everyone admires my curls. In reality, though, they weren't as good as they appeared. My hair was frizzy, dry, and I was dealing with severe hair fall. To address this, I had to invest in a good shampoo, conditioner, and serum. I can feel the change now. Although the before and after photos might look similar (I don't have a current picture), the difference is significant. Why would I showcase something that's not heroic? It wouldn't garner any views, right? Social media is a fraud. Influencers are fraudulent. The life they portray is a facade. I have a decent following here, and I know how easy it is to manipulate or present a false reality. So, don't be influenced by someone online. Don't despise your life based on a reel you just watched. Create your own story. Walk your own path. Be proud of who you are and take full responsibility for who you are going to become—on your own. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What life lesson did you learn the hard way?
Answer: Imagine playing Subway Surfers where the speed increases and obstacles become more challenging as you progress. It's thrilling and fun, right? Now, think about life. When the pace quickens and challenges arise, it often feels stressful rather than exciting. But what if we treated life like a game? In Subway Surfers the escalating speed and hurdles are what make the game exciting and engaging. We enjoy the rush, the need to stay sharp, and the satisfaction of overcoming obstacles. Life, in many ways, isn't that different. Challenges in life, much like in games, are opportunities for growth and learning. They push us to become better, stronger, and more resilient. Sometimes, life will be smooth, like a leisurely game session. Other times, it will throw countless hurdles our way, demanding courage and strength. Instead of dreading these moments, what if we welcomed them as part of the adventure? We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the single greatest piece of career advice, and why?

Saturday and Sunday were still vacant. I got up on Saturday. Made my bed. Cleaned my room. And washed all my clothes. I felt proud. The regular stuff but an achievement for me. Saturday night. Still no plans. I was bored. Bored to death. This was probably my first weekend in years without going out. I dreaded it. I slept at around 10:30 PM. Too early for me. I woke up late. I realised then and there that I needed to do something productive. I picked up a novel. The Silent Patient. I had 200 pages left to read. I've been reading this novel on and off for two months now. I felt ashamed. I felt guilty. I sat and finished it in one go. Bingo. I don't remember when I finished my last novel before this. I always skim through my old reads now. I couldn't complete any novel for months. This time, I did. Getting bored is necessary. When you're free, when you have a lot of vacant time, don't scroll through Instagram. Don't watch the YouTube shorts. Sit idle. Don't do anything. Sit idle until you're driven to do something productive. This has always worked for me. Don't be involved in a mess. Get bored. And get productive. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Why do I feel that everybody around me is fake?
Answer: I attended a funeral. My volleyball teammate’s mother had died. I called him two days before the incident. But he didn't pick up the call. I got to know why. We were fifteen people to visit his place after the volleyball match. That's when I got to know about the demise. My teammate wasn't there. He went to the market to buy some stuff for the antim yatra. And the moment he arrived, everyone rushed towards him. They started asking questions. Giving the gyaan that it happens. It's a part of life. And when he looked at me, I just looked back and said nothing. Everyone left after two minutes. I stayed. I stood near him. Sat near him. I didn't say a word. I listened. He's in his early 40’s and I didn't see him cry. I wasn't there to lend him a shoulder. I was there just to be there. Despite the age, he's more like a friend to me. I left after an hour as I had to login. I was there till his mother was carried to the antim yatra vehicle. The ones who left were mostly retired professionals or government employees. It was a public vacation that day. They were there just because they ‘had’ to be there. They wanted my friend to know that we were present. But what this ‘two minutes’ of presence means for someone whose mother just died, I don't know! I'm not the protagonist of this story. I'm not highlighting what I had done. I'm trying to question why faking a presence is required when you don't feel like it. I'm intrigued by death. I see it as the ultimate truth. I want to attend more funerals than marriages. It just humbles me down. But to someone who doesn't feel any empathy towards the other person, why does it have to be an obligation? Why do you have to visit a funeral just because you ‘have’ to be there? We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: If you could write a letter to someone you don't talk to anymore, who and what would you write?

And this bad touch memory of mine, it doesn't haunt me a bit.’ I went through a lot in my childhood. So much so, that I don't fear any situation or a person now. Not even death. I know for a fact that if I went through all of that at such a tender age, alone, and didn't jump from the cliff, I could face anything now. I don't want to lose that courage. I'm 26. Question: Why shouldn't you fall in love with writers?
Answer: I've never looked her beyond her eyes. It's not like I'm a saint. But I couldn't. The innocence in her eyes had never let me look beyond them. It never happened with any girl before. I don't know. It was strange. Whether she wore everyday clothes or an elegant dress, she was still the same for me. She might have looked into the mirror. She might have ruffled hair. She might have thought she was not the perfect girl for me. But she was. She still is. I still remember when we were crossing the road and she held my hand out of fear. That touch. That first-ever touch. It felt like a thunderbolt. My heart started sinking. A tear rolled down my eyes and she caught it. She knew I loved her. I could never confess my love for her. I could never tell that I didn't sleep the whole night just to wake her up for the gym. I couldn't tell her that I felt like beating the shit out of that gym trainer who passed her a smile. Every f*cking day. But, sometimes, it's too late. I loved her. She loved back, too. But it wasn't me. She was in a relationship, already, but I couldn't help my feelings. Such a sweet-hearted girl. Such a goddamn goddess. It never happened. Or even if it did, you'll never know. Writers can swiftly deny their story by saying it's a work of fiction. Or, they can write a fictional story to convince you that they are an ideal human being. We can fall for the writers, yes. Nothing wrong with that. But never fall for him ‘just’ because of his writing. Know him inside out. Some writers don't write what they are exactly. They write what they aspire to be. And, if you're wise enough, you must know that it could take him decades to be the person he aspires to be in his stories. The person you'll fall for and the real person aren't always the same. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Brag about yourself. What are you really good at doing?
Answer: Girls, brutal answer ahead. It was February, 2024. I went to a club with my flatmate and we were dancing. I saw a girl from a distance and she was cute. I gave her a smile. She smiled back and came towards the floor to dance with me. We started talking despite the loud music. She told me that she's from Punjab and she lost both her parents recently. I felt sad. The DJ played a Punjabi song and she started teaching me the moves. Just then, her friend came towards us and took her away. Her friend was angry with her. I went back to my friend but whenever that girl’s friend went to the washroom she came towards me and went back immediately because of her friend. It happened a couple of times when I went to her friend to talk in private. ‘See. She told me that you're like her elder sister and she's an orphan. She just wants to dance with me and I promise that I'll keep a safe distance with her. You can watch me. And if you see that I'm misbehaving, you take her away and I'll not say a word.’ Her friend started crying. She said she drank a lot. Her friends did, too, and she needed to take care of both of them. I suggested her to take both of them home, to which, she said let me order one more whiskey peg. I laughed from inside. As soon as the peg was finished, she smiled at me and took both of her friends home. The Punjabi girl and I exchanged numbers and planned to meet the next weekend. We did. It was ladies' night and drinks were free for her. She drank a lot despite me stopping her. So we went to another club where the drinks were paid. She started pleading that wants to have one more beer and I wasn't agreeing. Then she started hugging me. She was drunk. She placed a kiss on my right cheek and asked me to kiss her back. I said I will kiss you back tomorrow. Not today. It created a havoc. She was drunk. She won't leave me and knowing the fact that she was my responsibility, I couldn't just abandon her. So I asked for her address and booked a Cab. As soon as I booked the Cab, she started crying. She said she wants to go with me. She started pleading. She was crying. And I had a really tough time convincing her. I dropped her home. I called her roommate to come downstairs and take her to the room. The next day she texted me that she was drunk and apologized for her misbehaviour. I knew it. I was, and I still am, at a phase where I don't want any attachments. And that girl was innocent (as per my understanding). She was just highly drunk. This was one incident. I can give you many stories like this which might be triggering for you. It doesn't involve me. Still. Girls can't bear alcohol. And when they get drunk, they do things or allow things that they would regret the next morning. A harsh statement here: It's 100X easier for a guy to get into a girl's pants while she's drunk. So girls, please know your limits when you drink. And make sure you drink with the right person. Don't make a drinking plan with someone you don't know inside out. Even if it's casual, the other person could be a monster after drinking. I love honesty. I can brag about it as I've done it despite knowing the fact that it won't be good for me. I don't fear judgements. I've told everyone a thousand times over that I can give away my life for you in friendship but I’m horrible at romantic relationships. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

But this time, I felt more happy than ever. I didn't feel empty. I didn't feel like an orphan. And I knew I had to give away my personal secrets to give people strength. There's a thing about writing. The more personal you write, the more people will resonate with it and adore you for that. You saved my life, this statement, cannot be described in words. Neha, when she was going through her chemotherapy for her third-stage lung cancer, wrote your answers give me the strength to live. She couldn't make it, of course, as sometimes words are not enough. Question: What are the golden advices in life?
Answer: My Mama wrote a suicide letter. He was in his 20’s and he picked a brutal fight with his mom. My Nani loved him. Mama was the only boy she had. But fights are common in any relationship. My Mama took the fights personally. He locked himself in the room and wrote that if something happened to me, my mother would be the only person responsible. He thought Nani didn't love him. Everyone knew he would never take his life. He just wrote it out of anger. But he often did that. Saying that I will die. And, He did. He died when he was 27, meeting an accident. My Nani was shattered. She used to come home and cry to my mom. She would say I don't have the willingness to live anymore. I want to die. Everyone knew my Nani was very scared of death. She used to say it just because of her mental breakdown. Even after my Mama’s death, whenever she fell even a little ill, she instructed everyone to take her to the hospital. But she kept saying I want to die. Two years later, she did. My best friend's grandfather is in his 90’s. He forgets people. He can't walk properly. He's always ill. But the only thing he said throughout his life is I want to live more. Once he was so serious that his pulse dropped. Everyone thought he was dead. They took him immediately to the doctor and the doctor pumped air into his mouth. Guess what? He was alive. He was ready to live again. The question requires multiple advice but I'll state just one. You get what you say to yourself all day. So think twice before uttering anything. The subconscious is a deadly thing. Manifestation works. Destiny might take you there, and then, it will be too late to revert it. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the best way to get revenge on someone who broke your heart?
Answer: I'm an atheist who believes in books. If you talk against books, you'll have to pay a heavy price. There was a girl I met in the club. She was strikingly beautiful. There was a long eye contact between us so I went to her. She immediately said ‘Tanya’ and offered her hand for a handshake. ‘Shubham,’ I said, smiling at her. ‘Those curls are real?’ she asked. ‘No, no. These are only for picking girls in the club. I'm bald. Don't tell anyone.’ She laughed. She reached out for a chair and asked me to sit beside her. ‘You came so late to the club. It's almost 1:10 AM.’ ‘Yes,’ I said. ‘I was about to finish a novel. I was so hooked up that I didn't see the time.’ ‘Novel?’ she asked. ‘Yes. You love reading as well?’ ‘Who reads books nowadays? It's so boring. I hate books. Ewww.’ ‘Oh,’ I said. ‘Let's kill her now,’ my heart said. ‘Wait for it. Let me do something.’ my mind said. I started panicking. I started leaving and she asked me what happened. I said I lost my phone somewhere in the club. ‘Wait let me call you. Is your phone on ringing?’ she asked. ‘Yes.’ She took my number and called me. My phone rang. It was already in my jacket. I started laughing. ‘Nice way to get my number,’ she said, giving me a smirk. ‘Btw, what's that? The picture on your screenlock?’ I asked. ‘That’s a character from Naruto.’ ‘Naruto?’ I asked. ‘Yes,’ she said. ‘Don’t you watch Anime?’ ‘Oh, you mean cartoons? Okay, got it. No, I don't watch cartoons now. I used to in my childhood.’ She gave me a deadly stare. I didn't save her number. Said it was a pleasure meeting you. Went to the dance floor. And the funny part? The DJ was playing a song that said: Khoobsurat bahot tu hai lekin, dil lagaane ke kaabil nhi hai. The best way for a sweet revenge is patience. Don't react immediately. Wait for the right moment. Question: I don't want to get married, but I love my girlfriend. What should I do?
Answer: There's a movie on Netflix; Ok Jaanu. The female protagonist Tara had a gloomy childhood. Her father left them when she was just six years old. He never came back. This incident had a deep impact on Tara’s life and she decided to never get married. Then she met Aditya. A classy guy. Flirty. Not a typical guy to marry. But someone to fling around. They had a thing. They started roaming around with each other. They enjoyed their company. And they both had plans to go abroad after a couple of days. Different countries. So they decided to make the most of it. Aditya decided to move in with Tara at his uncle's house. His uncle was an old man, happily married to Charu Aunty, a lady who had a knack for classical singing. Charu aunty had Alzheimer's. She used to forget about people. She used to forget about where she was. But she would never forget that one person, Paplu, the nickname she had given to Aditya’s uncle. Gopi uncle (Paplu) took great care of Charu Aunty. He loved her so much despite what she was going through. Aditya and Tara, while witnessing that, started thinking in their subconscious that marriage isn't that bad. Then it was the time of separation. Aditya had to go to America. Tara had to go to Paris. And until now, they were in love with each other. But they decided to end it there and then. Until, of course, Charu aunty was lost. They started searching for her. She had gone outside home and Gopi uncle couldn't find her. Gopi uncle was crying. He thought he had lost her. Aditya and Tara were trying to search for her but it was not that easy. They even picked up a fight. Aditya realised that what if Tara goes through the same and there is no one to take care of her? He proposed. She said yes. They found Charu aunty. They took her home. And Gopi uncle started crying seeing her. Tara was scared of marriage. She saw a marriage that didn't turn out well in her childhood. And she didn't want to repeat it. But, of course, she fell in love. Love gives you the strength to eradicate your past blues. Love can change you. Love can bring the best in you. But you need to accept that. If you're afraid, if you can’t erase your past even if you have a beautiful present, you're making a mistake. Fix that. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are the best travel hacks?
Answer: This hack will change your life. But it will not be an easy one. The first thing you need to do is leave your comfort zone. And if you're willing to do that, please go ahead with this post. Travel solo. I can't emphasize enough on this point. Travel solo. Make your own plans. Select your favourite destination. And if it's your first solo-travel, make sure you go to a place that's already known to you. My first solo-trip was to Nainital. I had been to Nainital before that. And I knew about the place inside out. So when I went there, alone, I wasn't clueless. No one could fool me for the rates. Then, choose hostels. Always. They are cheap. You can get a bunk-bed under 500 on good days. Hostels have common areas where they have pool tables, table-tennis, and many other indoor sports. The best way to interact with strangers is to set up a match with them. Backpackers are friendly. Though the rates are cheap, you'll be amazed that people from top positions come there for solo-travels. Make plans with them. Go out with them. Talk with them. Save their contacts. It's fun. One day my sister sent me a reel on Women's Safety. The reel was a viral one. I saw it, and told my sister that the girl in this reel was my friend. I met her in Udaipur. We're now connected on WhatsApp. Didi was amazed. I've met many amazing people in my solo-travel. I joke around here and there all the time. And then comes the hard part. Move out. I don't stay in a hostel for more than two days. Even if I'm staying in the city for 10 days, I keep switching the hostels. This way, I get to meet more amazing people. More people, more insights. More insights, more stories. More stories, more memories. I don't make plans with them for my next trip. I always like to go solo. Try this. You need to leave your comfort zone for that. You need to have a good understanding of analysing good people from evil. And it comes from experiences. Explore it this way. And there's no coming back. (Solo trip to Udaipur) We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the biggest misconception people have about life?
Answer: Read any self-help book. Any. Most of them talk about the same thing. You should wake up at 4 AM. You should make a to-do list. You should read self-help novels. You should journal. You should build your own business. You should do this and that and only then you'll be happy. Now imagine a patient suffering from a disease. It would ideally take him six months to recover fully from just one medicine. But suddenly, a bunch of doctors suggests 40 medicines, thrice a day. Do you think his body will be able to take it? I'll be brutally honest here. Life is hard. It gets harder as you grow up as the number of shits you need to take increases exponentially. Sometimes, your heart will break so hard that you will think it's unrepairable. I've been there or maybe I'm still there and I can tell you one magical thing about life. It heals you slowly. You don't have to do anything. Life has a grandparent named Time and it heals you on its own. You might get new hardships. But the older ones get healed by themselves. But, in the process, you just need to do one thing correctly. Never Hate Yourself. Never do that. I don't care what makes you happy. It can be something like eating pasta. Or maybe a blueberry cheesecake. Get it. Be happy. You don't have to build air satellites to become happy. You don't have to wake up at 4 AM if you can't. You don't have to make a to-do list if not achieving it puts you in guilt. Enjoy the little things in life. Live on your terms. And give the biggest finger of your hand to people who judge you. Be supremely proud of yourself. Everyone wants to achieve great things. And they know what they should or should not do. So stop following the self-help advice if it's making your life more miserable. Smile. Smile for no reason. Smile by seeing a cute dog on the street or seeing a couple holding hands. Your time is clicking. Make sure you don't live with any regrets whatsoever. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are the really small things that tell a lot about a person's psychology and personality?

They have split personalities. You're on the receiving end for a couple of days and you term this person as CHARACTERLESS. Or a PLAYER. Or RUDE. Question: What is that one thing that you want to tell the world?
Answer: Delhi in January. It's devastatingly cold yet so beautiful. I love winters. And when the thought seeped inside my head that the winters are slowly going away, it broke my heart. I didn't go out in my favourite season. I locked myself in my flat for a week. I didn't go on a trip this month. I have been going on at least one trip a month for a year. And that streak is broken. I was awake one of those days, at 5 AM, when a thought started lingering inside my head. What's the joy of living? Why struggle and keep yourself moving when, ultimately, it's all going to end someday? I got scared. It took me a long, long time to drag myself from that self-hate a few years ago. And when I saw myself going into that terrain of thoughts again, I got afraid. I opened my inbox and thankfully there was a reel shared by my friend. I opened it and I knew it saved me. The reel was about a book. And everyone in the comments section was saying it was one of the saddest books they have ever read. I smiled. I ordered that book and my will to live increased exponentially. The book arrived today. And I can't explain how much this book means to me. I'm a sucker for dark books, and movies with a sad ending. I love them. It's not because I'm a sadist. But I haven't witnessed any fairy-tale yet so I have stopped believing in it. There was a time when I used to read romantic novels one after the other. I read it now as well. But I make sure they need to have a realistic ending. By realistic, I mean it shouldn't be a fairy-tale. Because life is anything but a fairy-tale. AT LEAST TO ME. I live for dark novels. I search them online whenever I crave for them. And trust me, every dark novel no matter how heart-wrenching read it is, teaches you a lesson. A lesson that you learn in a harsh way. This is my way of escaping the ill thoughts. I order a dark novel to heal myself. Iron cuts iron, right? So I cut down my self-hate thoughts by reading a sad book. And it has worked for me every time. Do you know what works for you? If not, please find it as soon as possible. Because someday, you might be that one thing away from saving your life. And. You will be proud of yourself for that. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What's the best compliment you've ever received? And who gave it to you?
Answer: She knew me. Just a ping on Quora and that's where it all started. A wonderful writer she was. She was, yes, as now she has stopped writing. I was in a phase where I wasn't responding to anyone's texts. I wasn't receiving any phone calls. But the moment I saw her text on Quora, I changed. I had been admiring her inspirational posts from a distance and then, I had a chance. But I was scared. I replied to her. We vibed. And I asked if we could talk on the call. She agreed. But the moment she picked up the call, I couldn't say anything. ‘I want to say something.’ ‘I know,’ she replied. ‘I’ve read almost all your answers and I know what you want to say. I promise that we're never going in that direction, ever.’ I laughed. It wasn't something I wanted to say. Okay, I wanted to say it but not on the very first call. Then, we started talking regularly. We met. I remember we met only when she used to be very disturbed from within. She was taking sleeping pills. She was into therapists. And when nothing worked for her, she used to ask me to meet me just to have a big warm hug. That's it. We never talked while meeting. Our meet never went beyond twenty minutes. We would meet. She used to hug me like a baby. Sometimes, she would cry and I used to console her. And that was it. We met quite rarely. About once in every four months. But, one fine day, she called me. ‘This needs to be said now. No matter how disgusting this might sound to you but I have no control over it. I like you. I like you more than I should. Maybe I love you. Or maybe I love you more than I should I love you. And the feeling, the feeling that you have this big gigantic rock inside your chest instead of a heart, it's killing me. You cannot love me. Leave ME, you cannot love anyone. And I don't know what to do about this fact as I'm at the receiving end now. You move mountains for me as a friend. And the thought of how much you can do for your girl, the girl you might love someday in the near future; it kills me. Because I'm not that girl right now. And I have no patience to keep waiting.’ I kept talking to her. I kept convincing her that she was thinking too much. ‘Thinking too much?’ she exclaimed. ‘Before I met you, I just admired you for your writing. But the very first time I met you, I looked into your eyes. They are beautiful in their own kind. But that's not it. Your eyes are the most enigmatic thing I've ever seen in my life. They speak. They want to say something. Something dark. I could never look into your eyes for more than five seconds. Ever. And the more I look away from your eyes, the more I fall in love with them. And you.’ She was right. This wasn't the first time someone was saying this to me. She knew this relation had come to a dead end. She said she had to let me go. It was good for both of us. So we parted ways only to never meet again. In an online or an offline world. It hurts. But I keep her words with me. Always Even on my toughest days. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Why is building Ram Mandir at Ayodhya so important for so many Hindus?
Answer: I'm an atheist. I might have zero knowledge of religion and God, but my common sense hasn't left me. I won't write that it would've been great if they built the largest hospital in Ayodhya. Or the biggest school for the poor. Because it can be done in any part of our country except Ayodhya, where the king of the Hindu religion was said to be born. Shri Ram, the God of the Hindu religion was living in his own birthland like this for 500 years: Now, you might be thinking how bullshit of an atheist I am, right? So here are the birthplaces of Gods of other religions (except Islam): Buddhism: Islam (pilgrimage site): Sikhism: Christianity: Now, if you compare these with the Ram Mandir before it was built, which was literally a tent, you will feel the logic behind it. But now, you might ask why there was so much hype about it. Why couldn't we build a simple temple as the God resides within us and what's the point of idol worship? So, the Ram Mandir that's been built in Ayodhya is not just about Hindus, it's about India. It's a historic event and it should be as beautiful as it can be. And no, I'm not a bhakt. I'll state my reason for the same: I went on a solo travel to Udaipur where I met a girl from North America. We used to roam around the city on a bike the whole day. One day, we went to the Karni Mata temple by Cable Car. We reached there and we could see the whole city from there. The view was amazing. We were standing next to each other, silently, when she said all of a sudden: ‘Shubham, this temple is so beautiful. Thanks for bringing me here. But I want to ask you something, I know for a fact that every God or Goddess in the Hindu Religion symbolises something. What does Karni Mata symbolise and when was this temple built?’ I couldn't answer that. But saying that I'm an atheist would've been foolish as I was standing there as an Indian. And it was a part of our history. So I said I'll look into it. Whenever I go for a travel, I observe foreigners are overly glad when see a historical temple. They want to know the story. And foreigners who visit India, they never say idol worship is bullshit. Instead, they pay 5x more than us just to witness it. Sometimes we need to shut our minds if it's being too intellectual for no reason. Things don't work ideally. Ideally, we should keep God in our hearts and shouldn't hang their photos on the wall. Yes. But why do we hang our parents' photos after they die? They are in our hearts, aren't they? It's okay to do things and believe in things that calm our minds and bring us peace. The country isn't going down because the government is building Ram Mandir instead of hospitals in Ayodhya. It's going down because we're our own enemies. Virat Kohli is an Indian cricketer. Do you know the country name that has the most active hate army of Virat or maybe Rohit Sharma? It's India. That's how it works here. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Do you have any advice for my early 20s life?
Answer: A mouse lived with me for ten days. He never appeared in the morning. But as soon as I went to sleep, he would enter my almirah and start nibbling the wood. The wood, yes. He didn't eat the wood, to be precise, he was just nibbling the wood to have fun. Which, as a result, didn't let me sleep. In the beginning, I enjoyed his game. I lived alone in my room and I had a new roomie. Wow. But then, it started affecting my sleep cycle. So I decided to catch him alive and throw him out of the house. Didn't work. None of my roomies were dumb. Neither was he. Sadly, I had to put a rat poison to get rid of him. It took me around ten days of improper sleep to send him to heaven. And those ten days, I thought they would never pass. But they sure did! One mouse, you see, it was just one mouse and I started hating my life. Alike mice, there will always be that one person in your life who will try to ruin your life. He can be anyone. Your friend. Your partner. Or maybe, just maybe, one of your toxic family members. Don't waste your time getting used to them. Or fixing your relationship with them. If it didn't work out for months and years, you wouldn't wake up, one day, and magically everything would get fixed. Things don't happen that way. Instead, try to maintain a fine distance from them. The early 20’s is the time when you’ll leave your college and start building your professional career. It's not easy. Don't let that one mouse spoil your beautiful beginning. Stay away. Maintain your distance. And wait, don't give them the rat poison. I never suggested that for humans. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What has your life taught you so far?

Question: What’s the best way to get over someone you love?
Answer: He was alive. I still remember when I pulled him out of the river. His body was cold. His eyes were closed. But he was breathing. I thought he was dead. It had been one hour of searching for him in the river. And there were zero chances that he could be alive. But… HE WAS BREATHING. My Nana (maternal grandfather) asked everyone to rush him to the hospital. We took him to the ICU where he was declared dead. He wasn't breathing. We thought he was breathing but he was dead long ago. He was my Nana Ji's only son. My mother's only brother. And the only Mama (maternal uncle) I had. He was dead. And I didn't leave his body until he was turned into ashes near the Ganga river. But this was just the beginning. I didn't sleep for days. Whenever I closed my eyes, he stood right in front of me. I was overly close to him. We used to play cricket together. We used to build an arena and play WWE. He used to carry me on his head while I was young. It wasn't easy to let him go. So I asked him to never leave me. I asked him to stay close to me. I asked him to AT LEAST come in my dreams every single day. And he did. It felt like he never left us. It felt like he never left his 2 y/o daughter. It felt like he was always there with us. But we all felt he wasn't at peace because his presence was slowly taking a mental toll on all of us. I scored a 4.2 CGPA in my third semester with two backlogs. I couldn't sleep in the darkness. And things had to change for good. I knew I had to let him go. I knew it was better for both of us. I knew he couldn't move on. I knew we couldn't move on. And maybe, he wanted one of us to say it out loud. So, one day, I sat down and talked to him. I said I want you to be in a better place. I said I want you to leave me and everyone close to you. That night, he came in my dream. I extended my arms to hug him. He was there, watching me. But he didn't come to hug me back. He vanished into the abyss. And… He never came in our dreams after that. Death has been a big fat mystery for me. I've been intrigued by death since childhood. And I was seeing all of this. It didn't feel real. It still doesn't feel real. It wasn't a fairy-tale goodbye. I couldn't even get my last hug. But it is what it is. One day or the other, you have to let them go. No matter how close they were to you, you have to let them go. It's better for both of you. It might sound harsh. It might sound selfish. But it is what it is. Let them go. And when someone talks about their problems, men think the other person really needs some advice. Nope. It doesn't work that way with women. Just be a calm listener. Be patient. Nod. Pat her. Question: What is a hopeless romantic and what does it feel like to be one?
Answer: I saw super cute bangles at Nahargarh Fort. I saw them and I was smiling like an idiot. I was with my roommate and his girlfriend was also there. I asked her to try it to check whether it will fit for my sister. It could have. But then, I dropped the idea. I wasn't going home any soon and I couldn't let those beauties remain in my room for long. There wasn't a second person I wanted to buy it for. No one comes even close. But then, I started to think of my future. I thought how beautiful it will look on my lover's slim wrists. I thought how cute those bangles will look while I'll be holding her little hands. And, I was now SMILING LIKE AN IDIOT! I had to stop. I felt like a fool. I decided then and there if I ever fall in love, the first thing I'd do is catch a bus to Jaipur and buy those bangles. I can travel for the whole day just to get her those cute bangles. And I realised the very moment that I'm in denial and I'm still a hopeless romantic. Being a hopeless romantic is like getting hit by a truck every day. You get hit by the truck of reality. You're lying on the road. BUT. You are smiling. You are smiling like the most stupid person on this planet. And you don't want to accept it. You go and stand in front of the truck every single day and people who see it can't fathom any logic behind it. Because there's no logic. Life doesn't give you fairy tales. BUT. I can. If I ever fall in love, like really really in love, I CAN give that person a novel-like fairy-tale. I know myself. But should you believe me? Should anyone ever believe a person who's a hopeless romantic? I reckon not. No one ever should. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What qualities of Indian Men attract foreigners?

I jumped onto the front seat. Then I started joking. I said I'll give you 2x money if you let me drive the auto. Then I told him jokingly that my ex left me for a pizza delivery guy. Everyone was laughing their hearts out. Just then, the girl from Chile asked the volunteers to take my picture with the bhaiya. She was so amazed. She kept asking everyone does everyone joke around and talk with the auto drivers. The answer was yes. Indian men don't leave a chance to talk with the auto walas, chai walas, and local vendors. The guy from Britain was also talking about it. I could see from their faces that they were impressed. The majority of Indian men are kind to people below them. Small thing. But okay! Question: What are the advantages of being selfish?
Answer: I cried my lungs out when my roompartner called me fake. He knew me for three years. And this was what I got in return for all the good things I did for him. BUT He was right. I'm still fake. I sometimes fake my kindness. I sometimes fake the good replies on Quora. I sometimes reply in the best possible way even when I don't feel like. I listen to people's problems. And even though my mind is about to burst, I'm patient like a wall. I've read many books on death and it helped me. No one wants to die being a jerk. When people know they are about to die, they BECOME kind. They want to be remembered as a good man. And so do I. When I die, I want to be remembered as 'Oh, that guy? He was the kindest soul I knew.’ We don't wake up one day and become kind. We need to practice it every single day. Even when we're feeling shitty. Even when our mind is about to explode. You shouldn't explode on others just because your manager is toxic. You smile. You help people. You become kind. Aren't we all dying? Aren't our days getting less? Don't you want to be remembered as a good guy? That's selfish, yes. But being kind doesn't harm anyone. Faking kindness doesn't harm anyone. It all starts will faking. And slowly, it starts running in your veins. You become humble. You become patient. You become the best version of yourself. (This book was written by a dying man. He had cancer. But the irony is everyone is dying. Everyone is inching towards death.) We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Are you worried that you will be single forever?
Answer: She had 120k followers on Instagram. I stumbled upon her profile I instantly realised I could walk a thousand miles for her. But it had to be different. Too many people were already hitting on her. I checked all her posts and most of her captions were shayaris. ‘Okay,' I said to myself. 'This is going to be hard. But let's do it.’ I used to wake up in the morning and send her one couplet of Urdu Shayari. The first day, she saw it but didn't respond to it. No worries. It went on for eight days until she heart-reacted to the Shayari. It was of Jaun Eliya. And I kissed Jaun Sir in the air. I continued. I never wrote anything else. No Hi's, no Hello's, just one poetry a day. She started liking all the messages after that. And, 27 days later, she sent me a Hi and liked my recent photo. 'Hi,' she texted. 'You have a good taste in poetry.’ I was jumping. I was already imagining her holding my hand. I was already imagining her kissing me slowly. I imagined how our kids would look like. BUT. IT HAD TO BE DIFFERENT. I didn't reply to her text and I kept on sending her shayaris. Now, the best ones. She texted me again after two days but I didn't reply. She gave up on me then. Or, I thought she did. I felt like a fool. It had been 144 days, now, and she wasn't liking the poetries or texting me. The days were tough. I thought it was not making any sense. Though she was reading the shayaris every single day. And putting them in her posts' captions. One day, when my patience was finally over, I sent her the shayari that was running in my veins. That I started to feel for her. So rahenge ke jaagte rahenge, Hum tere khwaab dekhte rahenge Tujhko choo ke kya hoga, Der tak haanth kaanpte rahenge. She read this. Head-reacted to the message. And called me on Instagram. I saw the notification. 'If I don't pick up the call, even now, it would be stupidity at its peak,' I said to myself. So I picked up the call. Shush. Nobody was saying anything. It went on for seconds and we both were loving that silence. The air around us was all lovey-dovey. And after, she finally said, 'Shubham, this trick of yours, if I'm the first girl you tried this on, I like you.’ I said yes, she was the first one. I didn't say I liked her, too, as it was definitely more than that from my side. Yesterday night, we were at India Gate. I hated the couples who kissed each other in public. And I never thought I could be one of them. But yesterday, I kissed her there. Not in the crowd. But a place from where we both could see the India Gate. I worried that I'd be single forever. But not now. We vibe so well. Touchwood. And I know you'll say I'm too crack to say it this early but; I want to marry her. I want to marry her as soon as possible. I've met a lot of girls but I never felt this for anyone. Seems like my story was pre-written. Wow. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Why should we do good?
Answer: Someone might be crying themselves to sleep every day. Someone might be suffering from an internal disease. Maybe their parents are toxic. Maybe their partner has cheated on them twice. But when they shout at you on a small thing, you can't see it. You won't get the backstory. You can't see what they are going through. A troubled person is rarely composed. So the next time someone shouts at you, over a trivial thing, and you're cool enough to give a smile and walk away, do that. We should always do good to people who are good to us, yes. But doing good to people who seem disturbed is heroic. You don't have to take so much in that it starts affecting your mental health. But if you can handle it politely, with a smile, you're a hero. Do good, without expecting anything in return. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Do more intelligent people tend to be more depressed?
Answer: Life is a slow suicide. This was said by Shiv Kumar Batalvi, the youngest poet to get the Sahitya Akademi Award. He died at a very young age of 36 and later received Padma Bhushan. No wonder, what he said was true. Every intellectual faces a slow suicide. It's inevitable. They read books that stab them. They watch movies that other people hate. And they question everything that's happening around them. People think you're crazy if you don't follow the herd. If you have different values, if you love being on your own, if you love locking yourself inside your room to read, everybody around will find you strange. People will start laughing at you. And you, as a result, will start hating this fake society. You will start hating these shallow people. You will hate their lavish lifestyle talks because it won't make sense to you. And you, eventually, would want to escape. You will die every single day. No wonder, why great writers like Ernest Hemingway, Virginia Woolf, and Sylvia Path killed themselves and writers like F Scott Fitzgerald, Charles Bukowski, and Raymond Chandler died out of alcoholism. Slow suicide. It has happened to a lot of intellectuals before. And it will keep on happening until we are here. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What makes you respect another person?
Answer: I think I'm broken beyond repair. I think my problems are apocalyptic. But then, a stranger walks into my life who's facing a problem that doesn't have any solution. His miseries have a dead end. He can't do anything about it. And he shares his problems, with me, with a broad smile. Oh my world! The calmness. The feeling that you're not alone. The feeling that no matter how big your problem is, somebody else is coping with that like a hero. Life is strange. It's not binary: zero or one. You deal with a problem and the day you think it's about to get over, you face another. This time, even bigger. But, sweetheart, you're not alone. You still have to suffer with that problem, yes. You still be crying almost every night, yes. But the moment you realise this world doesn't revolve around you, it gets better. You accept. You let yourself loose. Question: Do you fear death? Why or why not?
Answer: 3 AM, yesterday. I was walking in the jungle alone. I went to a party which was open till morning. There were many people there. I met a guy who was from Hyderabad. Such a lovely human he was. We talked about many things and danced together as well. I wanted to go back soon. Like, 1 AM or something. But he wished to stay there till 4 AM, at least. I agreed because I didn't exactly know the way back. But when it was 3 AM, it got too much for me. I was sleepy as I got a little drunk where you feel the buzz, but, you can take care of yourself. So, I decided to move out alone. The walk was beautiful. It was pitch dark. Everything nearby was invisible. And all you could see was your flashlight. Sometimes you could see a faraway hotel light. But that was all. But then, I got lost. I met the dead end of a mountain. I got scared. I started walking back to my party place again to go with that guy. I walked for only 10 minutes, around the jungle, and I knew he would be still there at the party place. Mid-way, before reaching the place, I met two guys who were heading towards my hostel. They said they were also coming back from that party. I got along with them and reached safely to my place. When I think of that instance, I know why didn't I think about death when I got lost. I was just scared of being lost in the jungle for no good. But I wasn't afraid of dying. I'm not suicidal. Neither do I fancy about an early death. I have just accepted the fact that when your time is over, you can't alter it. The fear of death won't let you experience a lot of things. Like, if I'd been scared of death, I wouldn't have done paragliding or bumpy jumping or that alone walk to the forest. I wouldn't have trusted those guys if I was shit scared of death. I don't fear death as it makes no sense. I try to be safe. But I don't get panicked over something which I have zero control over. (An amazing view from that walk. XD) We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What do you hate about people?
Answer: He was a labour worker. There was some work at my place in Gurgaon when my landlord called him up. I talked to him. I joked with him. And he did our work seamlessly. The next day, he was knocking on my door. 'Bhaiya, are you free?’ 'Yes, tell me. What happened?’ I replied. 'I bought a new phone and wanted to learn how to use WhatsApp and Facebook from you.’ 'Sure,' I said. 'Come inside.’ He smiled unexpectedly. He was about to sit on the faraway chair: 'Hey! What are you doing? Come here, sit on the sofa.’ 'But, actually… I'm drunk… so…' I said it was fine and he sat beside me. I taught him to use a mobile. It was a tough task, yes, but I tried to be calm and patient. When it was done and he was leaving, I asked his age out of nowhere. He was 23. I couldn't believe it. He was younger but due to hard labour, he looked way more older than me. We started to talk casually after that. He told me people are always rude to labour workers. Like, he said, a man kicked him yesterday just because he couldn't finish his work on time. ‘How could I?’ he replied. 'As it was raining the whole day.’ He didn't cry saying that. Everyone's eyes glitter up when they hear I travel solo. People look at me with admiration. They say I want to travel solo, as well, but I'm afraid of being bored. They say whenever I think of travelling solo someone accompanies me. I reply that the same happens with me but you need to say no. I planned this trip to Udaipur, solo, and when I told my plans to a girl, she asked if I was okay with her travelling with me. I refused politely. She's really sweet. A girl who gives you space and splits the bill. But I said I really like to travel alone. She understood it. Same happened with another girl. She said if you would've told me earlier I could have come along. Except, I don't want anyone to come along. I make friends in solo-travel. I go solo and when I return back, I have 40+ contacts on my mobile. That's crazy. I consider myself an introvert and that's really crazy. Solo-travel is all about living on your own terms. I slept enough so that I could function properly. I sat in the ghats on Udaipur, today, for three hours or so. And now I'm sitting on the rooftop, alone, with a view like this. Travel solo. It's addictive. And once you love your own company, you don't get hurt overly. Again and again. I've experienced this. And I don't want anyone to go through it no matter how me-centric this post sounds. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: How can I improve my writing skills?
Answer: My friend is an only child. He's a hundred women disguised in a body of a single boy. He talks a lot. He talks to an extent where you'd want to rip your eardrums off. When I asked him, jokingly, why do you talk so much, he replied: 'I'm an only child. My parents were mostly outside and I didn't have anyone to talk to. I was lonely. I used to talk to myself inside a closed room in my childhood.’ I felt so bad for him. I thought about it and I straightaway knew the reason why I've been writing so much for the past couple of years. Writing is a lonely process. Mostly, the writers are introverts who can't talk to anyone or don't want to talk to anyone. They are overwhelmed by the noises inside their heads hence they write. I notice new writers on Quora and their writing seems absurd. They have exactly the same thoughts as the flair writers here. They are as lonely as some of the brilliant writers, on Quora, but their writing isn't a magical spell, yet. It's more of a shout-out. A disarranged thoughts of the noises inside their heads. BUT. It gets better. I've been here for a long time now. I've seen writers going from absurd to wow. It doesn't happen overnight. It takes persistence. But it's possible. It keeps happening if people persist. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the best part of having a sister in life?
Answer: She was traumatized. A man was masturbating in the dorm above her. She was sleeping. And as soon as she heard ‘that’ voice, she came outside. I was sitting in the common area alongside other people. She came there and lit a cigarette. She looked anxious. 'What happened?’ I asked. And she started to narrate the whole incident to us. I was on a solo travel and made some friends on the very first day. We were five people, in total, two girls (including her) and three guys. When she was finished talking about the incident, we all started to discuss it. She was comfortable with us now. And we ended up talking and playing UNO for a long, long time. We sat there for the whole night as she couldn't sleep. She said she would be leaving that property as soon as the metro starts. When it was 6 AM and we were all sleepy, she thanked me before leaving. She said she could sleep now just because of me. She hugged me and made the checkout from that hostel the very next day. She lived in Gurgaon but I didn't ask for her number. I didn't help her because I wanted to impress her or something. I did it because I have a sister at home. Though I don't want any more sisterhood but I put other girls in my sister's shoes and do what I would've done for my sister in these scenarios. I even asked her to swap rooms if she was comfortable. Mine was an expensive room. I didn't want to impress that girl. Still, I did what I would've done for my sister. The most important thing about having a sister is you learn to respect girls. You can comfort them. You can make them feel safe. And, as per my understanding, that's the most important thing girls search for in a guy. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What advice would you give to an aspiring writer?
Answer: See this earthen pot. Say you fill it with fresh water. You keep it inside your room but you couldn't finish it. The water starts degrading. Now, you must drain the water out. And as soon as the water is drained, the pot is empty. An empty pot can catch dust. You must fill the fresh water again. That's exactly how a writer's mind operates. You can't write with an empty head. You should read a quality of good books in order to write well. You must fill the fresh water. And when you feel the thoughts are becoming overwhelming, when the water is degrading, when you can't handle the thoughts anymore, write. Writing is an extremely lonely process. The moment you drain the water, the moment you end up writing, there's a deep restlessness inside. The pot is empty and you feel a dark void inside. You can lose it. The pot might catch dust. And that's when you fill the fresh water again. That is when you read. You pick up a good book and fill your mind with thoughts. The emptiness is killing. You should regularly read in order to brim the water up. That's how it works. That's how writers keep on getting new ideas. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: For what have you lost hope?
Answer: I went out with a girl a few days back. This was our third meeting. I ordered a LIIT and she asked for a mocktail. 'I wanted to be sober, this time, to know a couple of things about myself.’ she said. 'Like?’ 'Do I really like you or is it just because I become drunk!’ 'What did you conclude then?’ I asked. 'It's the same. Feels like I'm still on alcohol. See! I say stupid stuff when you're around. I'm usually not like this.’ I smiled. 'I like it. You're very honest. You say things as it is.’ I said. 'By the way, we're spending a lot in these bars. Shouldn't we go out to cheaper places?’ 'Next time, sure, let's go to a beaten coffee shop.’ I said. 'I'm so glad you said it.’ 'Next time we're meeting at your place.’ she replied. 'Uh, let's see. I wanted to…' ‘Meet outside until you're sure, right?’ she asked. 'But how long are we talking about? How long will it take for you to commit?’ 'I don't know,' I said. ‘But I don't want to repeat the same cycle again and again. I want something else. I need to feel something else.’ 'I get it. But make sure we're not wasting each other's time.’ she replied. 'If you think it's a waste of time, if it definitely has to lead to something, let's be friends then. Let's not lose contact if you think it's not worth giving some time.’ 'I was not saying that. But still, let's be friends than making it more complicated.’ I've lost hope. People of my age don't want to waste their time. They want things quickly. Commitments. Promises. And relationship. There's hardly any time left after the work and if it doesn't look like going anywhere, why would they invest? I am, on the other hand, fed up with these flings. I can't fall in love that easily. I want to deep dive. I want to go to an extent where we literally crave each other. I want to make a connection that holds on for a long time. This wasn't me a few months back. Now, it has changed. I want to go slow. I want to talk. I want to go on a walk together. I want to travel and laugh and cry and do many other things before we are sure. I've lost hope in love. These metropolitans seem so fast-paced that it's hard to root for a novel-like love story. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What do guys really go through after a break up?
Answer: 'His girlfriend left him for a pizza delivery guy,' my friend said to a stranger. He laughed. Then we started joking around and a couple of people gathered in the Delhi metro. They thought we were funny and we had a youtube channel. Just then, I asked a guy who seemed drunk. His eyes were red and his shirt was tugged off. 'Have you ever had a breakup?’ 'Yes,' he said. 'Then this shayari is for you: “Mohabbaton mein dikhawe ki dosti na mila, Agar gale nahin milta to haath bhi na mila Khuda ki itni badi kaaynat mein maine Bas ek shakhs ko manga mujhe wahi na mila" He slowly clapped. I recited a few more shayaris, to him, when he decided to open up. 'I had two relationships, till date, and both girls left me. I'm a civil engineer. I have a decent job. But no one can assume it by seeing my appearance.’ When I asked him are you drunk, now, he said no. ‘I’m too sad to dress up or look good. Both the girls are married now. They both cheated on me.’ 'Reason?’ I asked. 'They never gave me the reason. They kept fooling me until I heard from someone that they are engaged or married. Both my relationships were quite similar.’ He was a year or two younger than me. He started asking me for advice. He started asking me that is there something you can tell me so that I can improve myself? So that no one will leave me again? ‘Yes,' I said. 'Just four lines. They have helped me a lot and it will help you also. Just remember this: “Kya dukh hai samandar ko bata bhi nahi sakta, Aansoo ki tarah aankh tak aa bhi nahi sakta. Tu chhod raha hai, to khataa isme teri kya, Har shakhs mera saath nibha bhi nahi sakta.” He smiled. We reached our metro station and I bid him goodbye. It was so heart-wrenching to just look at him. He was fighting a lot inside his head. He was going through an apocalypse. That night, I couldn't sleep properly. I thought about how soft men become once they fall in love. And how drenched in sadness when they are cheated upon. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Why do people who love reading, love it so much?
Answer: I'm sleep deprived. I want to sleep. I've turned on the AC and as soon as I turn off the lights, I crave a platonic touch. I want someone to caress my hair softly. I think about it and I can't sleep. I toss and turn on my bed. I turn for the last time and I see a book beside my cushion. I pick it up. I kiss it, gingerly, and I feel a wave of cool breeze on my skin. I'm having goosebumps. I know for a fact that when nobody's around, it is going to save me. It's not a prejudice. It has happened before. Whenever I felt I was falling into a dark abyss, there was always a book that came to my rescue. I have lost many people in this short life. A few of them have left this world and some of them have left me. There's a strange restlessness which comes with their memories. There's a deep scar. A terrible, invisible scar, that doesn't heal with time. Reading helps. It probably doesn't heal my scars. It just coats some beautiful colours on it. Question: What is the most beautiful thing in the whole world?

Your parents will appreciate you. Your siblings, your partner, or even strangers. You become different than before. But, for friends, you will always be the same. They will roast you. Make fun of you. Annoy you to death. They will be proud of your success, yes, but they will treat you just like before. And I love this, though, I haven't done anything extraordinary in life. I have a habit of reciting poetries to random strangers in the metro. When I do, they clap or appreciate me. That's where my friends come in. They say, ‘We wonder how you like the poetries, my ears are literally bleeding right now.’ I laugh at it. We laugh at it. For me, friendship is the most underrated and beautiful relationship of all. Whenever I think of not marrying, the only worry I have is not that I won't get any dates when I'll be in my 30s. What I fear, is, all my friends will be married by then, and they will not get enough time for me. Their priorities will change. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Am I a bad writer? My answers either don’t get upvotes or get low upvotes.
Answer: This is not Instagram. People don’t know you here. They are not your friends who will upvote your post just because they sympathize with you. Or want to support you. The rule on Quora is simple. If you can write well, your answers will start exploding after a point. It won't happen at once. It will happen, slowly, as the unknown readers need to trust your writing. Consistency also helps. Quora's algorithm treats you well if you write consistently. But once you stop writing here, it treats you like a beggar. But, above all, it's about what you write. Writing about microorganisms or crossword puzzles or binary series doesn't help on Quora. People come here for an escape. Write about human relationships, sadness, love, breakup, and novels. These are the evergreen topics. So, in case you're reading this, you're not a bad writer. Question: Why do we feel loneliness?
Answer: Infants cry when they're alone. But once they see someone, they stop crying. How many times we've seen babies dancing when they are around people? The same babies, when grow old, might love being alone than having people near them. The reason is simple. Humans are social animals. Since childhood, we enjoyed people's company. We always needed someone to play with. And when we grew up, when we realised that people haven't played with us but ‘played us', it broke our hearts. And we prefer being alone. No one loved being alone since childhood. There's a back story. Everyone has their past bruises that are still not healed. Everyone is hiding their sadness behind their lovely smile. When you've been hurt by people time and again, you sideline yourself. You keep everyone on the same spectrum. You think everyone's going to hurt you. And when they actually do, you become alone. Being alone was never in our genes. And when we're forced to live alone, and when that aloneness is filled with sadness, we turn lonely. Though it's a disastrous thing. But it's not permanent. We're lonely when we don't accept our aloneness. ...

Question: Do you prefer to speak English or Hindi at home and why?
Answer: I went to Starbucks for the first time yesterday. I was adamant about never visiting that place, even once, as I've heard it's overhyped. But my friend insisted to give it a try. 'The bill is on me.’ he said. 'Even then, no.’ I replied. 'Just once? Please don't say no!’ 'Okay, cool.’ He went on to give the order and one cold-coffee costed us around 400. Woah! The guy at the counter asked: 'Would you like to have anything else, Sir?’ 'That is all,' I said. 'Can I ask you one thing if you don't mind?’ 'Sure.’ 'Don't you guys know Hindi?’ He smiled. He said we do know Hindi but the customers here talk mostly in English so it became our habit, too. 'But,' he said. 'English doesn't have that feel. If given a chance, I'd any day prefer to communicate in Hindi. It's so beautiful. It gives you the feeling that you're talking to your people.’ 'I agree,' I replied. 'Whenever I'm outside and someone talks to me in English, though their mother tongue is Hindi, I feel like I'm still at the office.’ He laughed. We had a good talk afterwards and I came out of Starbucks only to decide that I'm never going back there, anymore. 'All these fancy shops make you feel good. You tell someone you're at Starbucks and it will give make you feel good. That is it, I guess.’ I said. 'Agree,' my friend replied. 'Even the language,' I said. 'Where's the need, actually? You two are best friends. You both grew up speaking Hindi. And all of a sudden you see it's not the trend and you adapt. You're talking in a foreign language even when you're behind the closed doors. Even when no one's watching you.’ We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Many famous writers having 2x or even 3x followers, than me, unfollowed me after a while. They had their reasons and I have zero hatred towards them. A doubt, maybe, but no hatred. I hate to say this but 'I often skip my Quora inbox’. Sometimes, I'm too low to have a conversation or to give someone a reply. So, I try to extend it a bit. When I come back and reply to them after a couple of days, I see they have unfollowed me and they are not here anymore. I don't get upset about the unfollowing part, now, but I do regret not replying to them earlier. But, then again, I like to keep myself at the priority. That's how you save yourself by keeping at least some hours, a day, for yourself. I really don't mind someone unfollowing me. If you don't like my content, unfollow me or even mute me so that I can't dance in your feed. If you like my writing style, but hate me as a person, what you can do is just read my answers and don't follow me. You don't even have to upvote my answers. Take your time until you change your mind. If not, you can go on reading like that, I won't mind (because I won't know XD). As long as I'm beneficial to at least one person, on Quora, I might come and pen my thoughts down. If not, I'll accept that my time is over and let's just watch new writers shine from a corner without telling them the truth. The truth, that, no matter how many followers you have, if you're alone and it's killing you, you're not going to open up to any one of them. You'll die. You'll be called a good man. And you'll be forgotten after a couple of days or months or at max, a year. (People who're tolerating me for so long deserve this virtual brownie). We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the most beautiful compliment you ever received?
Answer: 'What do you like the most about me?’ 'You mean, just one thing I like the most about you?’ she asked. 'Yes,’ I replied. ‘Okay, let me think…’ she said and started mulling over the question. 'Okay, I got it.’ she said. 'Say it.’ 'Your… you know…' she said, and started laughing like an idiot. 'No jokes, please. I'm asking you literally. I need to know this.’ 'Sorry, sorry…' she said, ‘So, it'd be your affinity toward books. The way you treat them. You don't underline anything on them just to keep them fresh. You don't fold them. You like to sleep with them. The way your eyes glitter up talking about the writers. The way your soul shatters when someone asks for a book from your book collection. But, at the same time, the way you've gifted dozens of books to people. I like when you talk about books.’ 'I mean, really? My love for books is what you like in me, the most? Why?’ I asked, puzzled. 'Because it makes you happy. You become a kid when you talk about books. I really like that side of yours.’ I hugged her and said you're weird, in a very cute way. She nodded and hugged me back, even tighter. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What did you learn too late in life?
Answer: A few days back, my friend and I were out of options. We went to a restaurant where he ordered a Hyderabadi chicken biryani. And I ordered a veg biryani. I couldn't finish it. For a person who hates wasting food, it was a really rough patch. I quit chicken a year ago. Chicken biryani was my favourite dish back then. But one day, all of a sudden, I felt like quitting chicken. And I have never touched it after that. When someone asks my favourite dish, even now, I tell them it's Biryani. Chicken Biryani. But the inner voice doesn't let me have it. I have zero judgements for people who eat chicken. I think they are lucky. It tastes well and it's healthy, as well. But I had started eating it for minimal price protein intake in my college days. And once I had started earning, and joined the gym, I quit it. I miss it now. The craving's there sometimes. Question: What are the small, tiny, little instances in life that give you happiness?

Question: What kind of girls do guys fall for?
Answer: I saw a girl wearing a black salwar-suit, with coloured bangles, decorated earrings, and a teeny-tiny bindi. She was beautiful. Okay, she was not beautiful. She was mind-blowingly gorgeous. And…and...SHE WAS LOOKING AT ME. Still, that was okay. The sight wasn't good enough, for me, to avoid reading my book in the metros. The thing I love the most. I opened my book and started reading. I had planned to finish the book, on the metro, and I was progressing really well. But then, I heard someone telling her breakup story. 'He was so toxic that despite having a job he used to ask for money. I had to take extra money from my parents.’ A girl sitting beside her was telling her story. The girl-with-coloured-bangles was continuously listening. Nodding. Listening. Nodding. And when it was her time to add up something, the other girl won't let her speak. She kept on speaking (the other girl) until her metro station was there. But the girl-with-coloured-bangles was listening, patiently, like a wall. In the meanwhile, of course, SHE WAS LOOKING AT ME. I absolutely adore girls who're great listeners. But, I had to complete my book. I started reading, again, but when I craned up, she was having a book in hand. A beautiful girl with a book in hand, save me, please! I looked at her. She looked at me. And I was melting despite the metro swaying chilled waves. I HAD TO COMPLETE MY BOOK. I was determined. I picked up my book, yet again, and resumed reading. I was there. Almost there in the last few pages. But then, my friend said something and I replied to him. I had the urge to look forward. When I did, she had a diary in hand with a sketch pen. She was sketching something. I told my friend about her. I told her how artistic girls pull me like a magnet. He smiled. I gave up on reading. I started talking to my friend, and concurrently, I was noticing her. We were having that eye contact. That eye contact where you know you like each other and it's going to last. I thought about my past experiences, with girls, and thought about dropping the idea to look at her. But then, just then, she took out a pen and started writing in her diary. WRITING. Someone got to be kidding me. A girl who reads. A girl who sketches. A girl who writes. A girl who looks as beautiful as she can be. A girl with a traditional dress. A girl with such alluring eyes. A girl. That girl. Such girls. OH MY WORLD! We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are the advantages of being lonely?
Answer: It's a lovely feeling. I was talking to an old man who had a tea shop in Nainital. His shop was always occupied. But one day, while I was sightseeing, alone, it started raining heavily. I parked my rented Ntorq and went to the stall. I asked for a coffee. And since there was no one there, except me, that old man started talking to me. 'So, where did you come from?’ he asked. 'MP. I live in Madhya Pradesh.’ I said. ‘And you're with?’ 'Myself. I came for the solo travel.’ I said. 'That's great, beta,' he replied. 'At least you're enjoying yourself, alone, other than the youngsters who take sleeping pills or take anti-depressants when they feel lonely.’ 'Haha, thank you, uncle. To be honest, I also feel alone and lonely and depressed. But it's just that, these days, loneliness has become an addiction. It brings joy to me.’ 'You enjoying being lonely?’ 'Sort of, uncle.’ I said. 'I like the feeling where you feel extremely low and melancholic but you choose to discover yourself instead of taking the pills to sleep. You choose to turn that loneliness into solitude. For me, reading helps like magic.’ 'My son hates books. He never studies though he has all the perks he can have.’ 'I hated books, too, while I was in school. I started loving them once I needed them. XD.’ I replied while sipping the last bit of coffee. The rain had stopped while we were busy talking. Or, I was busy talking. I gave him a hanger-wide smile. And went more up, on the mountains. We all are gifted, Shubham KP
