Question: Who can write something random here?
Answer: I hate to write this but well, let's do it. I'm a narcissist. I self-sabotage myself a lot. And I call myself weird before anyone else could even realise that. But, I love this one thing about myself. I'm brutally honest. I haven't fooled anyone. And when I say anyone, that includes that one girl I've written a lot about on Quora. That girl, who's the most beautiful human being I have ever met from Quora. And the only person I've met from Quora so far. She knows everything about me from scratch. She knows my back story. She knows about my childhood traumas. And she knows what I've been through. I waited for twenty-four years before I could even touch a girl. I waited for twenty-four years hoping that I'd fall in love. Sadly, I didn't. I thought I'd never found the right girl. But when I found her, I thought that was her. I told her everything. I told her it was a terrible idea to date me as I can't fall in love. To which, she said that's okay. She said that's completely fine as all we could do right now is being together. She knew there was something wrong with me. She knew there was some reason behind everything. And all she said was, if you ever want to open up to someone, whenever you think that secret of yours… if you can't take it anymore, you can share it with me. It took me one year, almost, to tell her everything while crying my lungs out. I was deeply connected with her. I never touched any girl other than her. But one day while we were laying on the bed, she whispered I love you in my ear, and it changed everything. She was okay with that feeling not being reciprocated. She said I know you can't fall in love and why you can't fall in love, and I have no issues with that. But I couldn't live with that feeling. But I couldn't live on like that. We got separated after that. And I started to exploit myself afterwards. I'm on an extremely lonely path. I can't see a future with anyone no matter how beautiful the person is, inside out. And that, my friend, comes with a back story. I hate marriage. Hate is a big word, I know, but that's how I have always felt. She knew this, too. I have never kept her at bay. We're still in contact. She still thinks I'm the most beautiful human being she has ever met. And when I ask her what can I change in myself to become a better person, she says, NOTHING. I never wanted to share my personal story here. But when you have constant readers who might get wrongly influenced by you, or they think doing wrong can be justified, you have to come up with a story that's not fiction. This is my story. Here's what it takes to be me. And if you think that a known writer's bed is full of roses, you're mistaken. I sometimes wonder if someone has to live in my shoes for once, will they be able to survive? I don't get an answer. But again, I don't want someone to trade shoes with me. It's quite disastrous out here. It's a daily nightmare. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Is it bad to read too many books?
Answer: Yes. I read too many books. I buy more books than I can read so that I'm never out of books. And when I'm feeling too low, I grab a book without a second thought. Yesterday, I went to a bookstore and I saw a book by Ernest Hemingway. It was costing me around 100rs more than the online price. I don't like calling someone and saying: 'Hey, I was feeling very low. Can you please talk to me for an hour? Can you please stay on the call?’ I've had bad experiences with people on this front. Whenever I was low and needed some help, people were busy. And I have no hard feelings for them. Everyone is busy these days. And that's why I rely on books. The worst thing about reading too many books is you become self-centred. You don't need people. You like spending time with people, yes, but you like spending time with books more. Because, of course, it never lets you down. Reading too many books hampers your human relations, yes, but then again, it also keeps you alive! We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Are you a solo traveller?
Answer: This is my fourth solo-trip in 2023. And that's all I have. I have started exploring solo-travel this year and I regret being so late. However, I've begun. I remember travelling with my friends and family before this year. It was fun, yes, but that was it. There wasn't self-discovery, serenity, being-in-the-moment, and the most important part… freedom. When you travel solo, there's no rush to cover all the places. You go to a place and if you like it, you can stay there as long as you want. You're the master of your journey. I hated the moment so much when I was at a scenic place and I was asked to click the pictures all the time. And once it was done, you need to get up and start moving. It hurts sometimes when I'm at a lovely place, solo, and I can't take a picture of myself. But that's okay. Who's there to impress, right? But if the feeling is too strong and you find someone around you, you can always ask them to take a picture of you. No one refuses. The only requirement of travelling solo is you need to love yourself. You must know how to spend time with yourself. And if it's getting too overwhelming, you can always carry a book. I have four. XD. And I know they won't let me down. (The Red Fort being a part of my journey to the mountains XD) We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What's the point of living if it's just an endless cycle of suffering?
Answer: My brother is in the Army. The training often gets overwhelming for him. On top of that, he loves a girl but she’s from another cast. He wakes up sleep-deprived. His parents do not agree to the marriage due to societal pressure. His parents aren’t totally at fault, too. They are connected to rural life. And if my brother gets married to a girl from another caste then his sisters won’t get married. It’s their rule. The rule of the society. His parents are worried about the girls in their family. And, it is justified. What’s more, is, if this marriage happens, then no one in his village will visit their parents and grandparents. The people around will simply break all contact. It’s that serious. My cousin, he’s two years younger than me, and he loves his family as well as that girl. But since things are going haywire, he calls me whenever the sufferings brim his head. Whenever he can’t take it anymore. My masi called me this Sunday, while I was travelling in the metro, asking me to talk to my brother as he needs some motivation. ‘Needs some motivation, wow!’ I said to myself. ‘Motivation from a guy as ordinary as me.’ I too suffer from the daily blues. I too can’t take it anymore, sometimes. And when I do, when I think about what’s the point of living this shitty life, all I think about is the people who look up to me. I don’t want to end my life, giving the hope to people near my vicinity, that ending your life is the best possible escape. If I end my life, it’s not just one casualty. It can be two. Or three. Or maybe more. I sometimes think how good it would’ve been if people didn’t know that they can hang themselves. I sometimes think how good it would’ve been if people didn’t know that something like suicide really exist. Long story short, we all are tiny pieces of shit. We wanted to make it big but we’re living an ordinary life. But that’s okay. We don’t need to look at the past. We don’t need to look ten years from now as it might seem gloomy. All we can do is, take one day at a time. One day at a time until our destiny starts to explode. Until then, dress up, work on ourself, and be proud of what you really are— at the present. Don’t wait to embrace the (future version) of yourself. Embrace yourself now. Because, if you won’t, I might start crying. Do you want me to cry? We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are some small things that you miss the most in your life?
Answer: 'Why are you crying?’ she asked. 'Nothing.’ 'Hey, Payal, see Shubham is crying.’ 'You idiots,’ I said. ‘I'm not crying. It's just the dust.’ I went to the terrace. My eyes got welled up with tears and when I returned, they had the same question. I had to answer them now. I couldn't run away from it. 'I miss my mother. You need to come out of your home. You have to meet new people. Being at home, it makes you a sloth.’ 'Justified. But did you explain this to her?’ 'Yes.’ 'And what did she say?’ 'She said your friends are also here. To which, I replied, that everyone is gone now. But what she said next was...’ I said, and my voice crumbled. 'Yes?’ she asked. 'She said you can make new friends here if your childhood friends are gone. This is impossible, right? But the way she said it, I knew it was her love, for me, that was speaking. She had never said anything like that before. She... she never holds me for anything. But this time, she did. And I can go back home, yes, but my colleagues have already started to go to the office. ‘I will have to go, as well,' I said. 'Some day or the other, I need to join the office. That's why I'm taking a flat in Gurgaon. But with my parents getting old, and my sister about to get married, it becomes tough. 'On the roads, while walking.’ 'You crazy?’ 'You're a fattu. Nothing will happen. And even if it does, I'll take care of that.’ I went to the shop and bought two Budweiser Magnum. We started drinking it on the roads. Then we sat near a villa and I finished my Can. Hers was remaining. We stood up, again, and started walking. She asked what was troubling me. She said I seemed lost. 'In the texts,' I replied. 'No,' she said, held my hand, and asked me to sit on a bench. 'Tell me right now or we're going nowhere.’ 'Your wish. 'All four of your friends can't be wrong.’ She booked a cab. And when it was there, almost, she cancelled it. She didn't want to go. She said she'd be walking home. I accompanied. We kept walking. The roads were dark. There was a place that was totally unlit. She held my hand and pulled me into the corner. 'Not here,' I said. 'Someone might see us.’ 'Fattu,' she replied. I held her. I gave her a warm hug. She hugged me like a child, as if her life depended on me. She started walking again when she said she wanted to kiss me for the last time. That's really a bad idea, I said, but she pulled me. I rested my lips on hers and we kissed. I separated her as I was afraid. We bought ice cream. We reached her flat but I didn't say anything. I kept it to myself. I booked my Rapido. The guy arrived while I was brushing my fingers on her shoulders. Okay, I said, it's time to go. She stood up and went towards the main gate. Like that? I said. But she didn't bulge. We didn't hug. She was too angry to give me a goodbye hug. Yet, I didn't say anything. That's what I did tonight. And that's what I always do. I upset people to the core. I'm weird. Like, really really weird. Why? I know but that's the secret to keep right now. We all are gifted, Shubham KP
